harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, proved the kernel OOM killer spares it and kills an unprotected memory-hog process instead, then completed the mandatory single-node restart/recovery protocol.
actions_performed: Created system user 'inventory' and directories /opt/inventory-api, /var/lib/inventory-api
Wrote /opt/inventory-api/app.py: a threaded HTTP server with /health and /inventory JSON endpoints, persisting data to /var/lib/inventory-api/inventory.json
Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service (Restart=always, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 to exempt it from the kernel OOM killer) and enabled+started it
Verified baseline health via curl and captured pre-test boot_id
Disabled swap (swapoff -a) to make real global OOM triggering fast and deterministic (swap was later restored)
Launched an unprotected memory-hog (systemd-run transient unit 'memhog', default oom_score_adj=0) that allocates and touches memory until exhaustion

Polled memory usage, memhog status, and inventory-api health during the OOM event; confirmed via dmesg that the kernel's global OOM killer selected and killed PID 1811 (memhog, oom_score_adj=0) while inventory-api (PID 1717, oom_score_adj=-1000) stayed active and kept answering /health throughout
Re-enabled swap (swapon -a) and cleaned up the transient hog unit/script
Captured pre-restart boot_id, enabled/active state, and live health/data response
Rebooted node1 via 'sudo -n reboot' (acknowledgement returned before disconnect), polled until exec connectivity returned

Verified boot_id changed post-reboot, confirmed inventory-api auto-started (enabled, active), OOMScoreAdjust persisted at -1000, /health and /inventory (with original persisted data) responded correctly, and swap was correctly restored

evidence.requirement: inventory-api deployed as a managed (systemd) service, healthy baseline before disruption
evidence.summary: systemctl status shows inventory-api.service active/enabled with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 (oom_score_adj -1000 confirmed on the running PID); curl /health and /inventory succeed; boot_id 368725cb... captured as pre-test baseline

evidence.requirement: Memory-hungry process drives system out of memory and is the process the kernel stops, while inventory-api keeps serving
evidence.summary: memhog launched with default oom_score_adj=0 (unprotected); polling shows memory climbing to 1.7Gi/1.9Gi then memhog going inactive; dmesg shows 'Out of memory: Killed process 1811 (python3) ... oom_score_adj:0' matching memhog's PID; inventory-api remained active and /health returned pid=1717 with growing uptime throughout the event

evidence.requirement: System restored to normal (swap re-enabled, service still healthy) after the OOM demonstration
evidence.summary: swapon -a restored 2G swap (0 used), inventory-api still active, /inventory returns correct persisted data

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id=368725cb-c64e-4393-b25f-da5111703b4a captured; inventory-api confirmed enabled+active with working /health and /inventory responses

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect, node restarted one at a time
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sudo -n reboot' returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately; next exec call failed with connection reset, confirming the node went down after acknowledgement was returned

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: proof of changed boot identity and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: Connectivity returned after polling; post-restart boot_id=cfb8c08c-cf89-4629-9754-e78e3d56fea2 (different from pre-restart value), uptime -s confirms fresh boot; inventory-api auto-started (enabled/active) with OOMScoreAdjust still -1000, /health and /inventory both serve correctly with persisted data, and swap is correctly present (2G, 0 used)

attempts.summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, proved the kernel OOM killer spares it and kills an unprotected memory-hog process instead, then completed the mandatory single-node restart/recovery protocol.
